correctness.rationale: Endpoint conditions are exactly ∫u=-1 and ∫t u=0. For the mean -1 and |u|<=U, rearrangement against the switch point τ=(U+1)/(2U) shows the maximum first moment is U(1−2τ²)/2, giving U>=1+√2 for feasibility (U<1 is trivially impossible). A convex interpolation yields admissible moment zero. For nondecreasing u, derivative μ=Du≥0 has mass T=TV(u), and eliminating the initial level gives ∫s(1−s)dμ=1. With m=∫(1−s)dμ∈(1,U−1], Cauchy gives T>=m²/(m−1), minimal at m=U−1 in capped regime U<=3, equality forcing μ to one atom. For U>=3, s(1−s)<=1/4 forces T>=4, attained uniquely at s=1/2. Independently verified symbolic switch moments, cap threshold and saturation-branch continuity at U=3 and sampled caps; analytic inequalities cover all functions and cap values.
